assessment.summary: TREM2 is a well-validated immunoreceptor target with strong structural characterisation (15 PDB structures, best resolution 1.47Å, 11 ligand-bound) and robust disease association in Alzheimer's disease, neurodegeneration, and cancer immunology. However, chemical tractability is currently low with zero IC50 entries in ChEMBL, though very recent (2026) preclinical and first-in-human data for an oral small-molecule agonist (VG-3927/SAR448851) suggests the target is actively being pursued and may soon acquire meaningful chemical data. Overall druggability is rated medium, reflecting strong structural and biological validation offset by a near-absent public small-molecule dataset.
evidence_gaps: No IC50 or bioactivity entries in ChEMBL for this target despite emerging small-molecule agonist programmes — public chemical data is essentially absent
No approved drugs; clinical-stage molecules are very early (first-in-human 2026)
Mechanism of TREM2 agonism via small molecules is not yet well characterised in the public domain — binding sites and SAR are largely proprietary

AlphaFold pLDDT is moderate (76.8 mean, 61% >70) suggesting some structural regions, potentially the transmembrane/intracellular region, lack high confidence — may limit full-length druggability modelling

Context-dependency of TREM2 signalling (neurodegeneration vs. cancer, agonism vs. antagonism) means the therapeutic modality is not yet settled — different disease indications may require opposing pharmacologies
No published clinical efficacy or safety data yet for any TREM2-directed small molecule
